html:
A town founded by the French in 1659 on an island at the mouth of the Senegal River, the first permanent French settlement in West Africa.

It traded gum arabic, gold and slaves from upriver. A society of Afro-French families grew there, led by wealthy women traders called signares. Saint-Louis was the capital of the colony of Senegal and of French West Africa until the government moved to Dakar in 1902, and the capital of Senegal until 1957. It was one of the Four Communes whose people could vote for the French parliament. Its colonial quarter is a World Heritage Site, now threatened by the sea. See also Faidherbe.
sum: A town founded by the French in 1659 on an island at the mouth of the Senegal River, the first permanent French settlement in West Africa.
